clue.text: Flag by the end of gloomy game

indicators.note: the flag word is placed beside the close of the gloomy word, so it comes after it

parts.note: gloomy means black, as in a black mood
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A flag flown beside a gloomy scene, as if signalling the end of some sombre game.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack is the card game also called pontoon or twenty-one.

clue.text: Sure United will be involved in tie

indicators.note: the letter for United is caught up inside the word for tie

parts.note: a bond is a tie or link
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: United will feature in a cup tie, that's certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound in 'bound to win' means certain or sure to happen.

clue.text: Berkshire village an old master portrayed originally

indicators.note: an original portrayal of these words redraws their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A Berkshire village first painted by an Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERMASTON is a village in Berkshire, an English county west of London, known for its atomic weapons site and 1950s protest marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermaston is a real village in the county of Berkshire, home of a nuclear research establishment.

clue.text: Turkish capital left by first couple meeting Greek character in port

indicators.note: the first two letters abandon the Turkish capital

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Travellers leave the Turkish capital and meet a Greek figure in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi is the chief seaport of Pakistan, on the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Records in waste briefly turning up outside busy place

indicators.note: the reversed waste word goes outside the busy place
in a down clue, turning up means the letters read upwards, reversed
briefly means the waste word loses its last letter

parts.note: scrap means waste or rubbish
a hive, as in a hive of activity, is a busy place

explanation.surface: Records left as waste outside a busy office.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical records and documents.

clue.text: Stunner goes round one day in exotic dress

indicators.note: the knockout abbreviation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a KO, or knockout, is a stunning blow
I is the Roman numeral one
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A stunning woman twirls round one day in an exotic gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beautiful woman, but here it is a knockout punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is the traditional Japanese robe, exotic to Western eyes.

clue.text: Baby's pram initially covered in dirt

indicators.note: the opening letter of pram is wrapped up inside the word for dirt

parts.note: soil is dirt or earth

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of pram

explanation.surface: A baby's pram is caked in muck after a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' looks like a noun but is the verb: to baby someone is to pamper them.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby a child is to pamper or indulge it too much, which ruins its character.

clue.text: Officer perhaps flogged strapping individual losing head

parts.note: flogged is slang for sold

indicators.note: the strapping individual drops its first letter

parts.note: a tier is one who ties, as with straps

explanation.surface: An officer flogged a strapping recruit, who then lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' means sold in British slang, not whipped; 'strapping' means binding, not burly.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is one example of a member of an army, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Witchcraft portrayed by Holbein regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks out every other letter of Holbein, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Sorcery seen in a painting by Holbein.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, or obeah, is a form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Best, but not the first, meeting, strictly speaking

indicators.note: the word for best loses its first letter

parts.note: the elite are the best
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Strictly speaking, the best meeting was not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally means in the exact, word-for-word sense, without exaggeration.

clue.text: Smaller than some European articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a word for 'a' used by some Europeans
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: A shopper finds some European goods are smaller than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are articles in the grammatical sense: French UN ('a') and German DER ('the').
explanation.definitionFit: Under can mean less than, as in under ten pounds, so it stands for a lower amount or size.

clue.text: In court rejected second apparent objection

indicators.note: the following pieces sit inside the court abbreviation
rejected means the word for a second is turned back to front

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
plain means obvious or apparent

explanation.surface: A lawyer in court has a second objection thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a protest or grievance raised against something.

clue.text: Order device primarily used in more precise navigational aid

parts.note: a direction is an order or instruction

indicators.note: the first letter of device is set inside the word for more precise

parts.note: finer means more exact or precise

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter of device

explanation.surface: An order to use a device in more precise navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: This radio instrument works out the bearing of a transmitter, helping ships and aircraft navigate.

clue.text: Joining party in poor health after check

indicators.note: the word for poor health is placed after the word for check

parts.note: a do is a party
to vet is to check
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone joins a party while unwell after a medical check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dovetailing means fitting together neatly, like interlocking joints in carpentry.

clue.text: Sweets moved about near lips

indicators.note: the letters of near lips are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sweets are moved around close to someone's lips as they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pralines are confections of nuts cooked in caramelised sugar.

clue.text: Condemn act of piracy in plain language

indicators.note: the piracy word sits inside the plain language word

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing as opposed to verse
a crib is a copy, piracy of someone's work

explanation.surface: Someone condemns piracy in blunt terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or denounce something officially.

clue.text: Line on chauffeur's pants

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting the line on means placing it after

parts.note: a chauffeur's job is to drive

explanation.surface: A line drawn on a chauffeur's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish or nonsense, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang 'pants' means nonsense, which is what drivel is.

clue.text: Impression of Oxford? Once Labour leader's flipping favourite

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

indicators.note: flipping means the favourite word is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: An impression of an Oxford don and a former Labour leader's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced shoe, so its impression is the mark it leaves, not a mimic of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford shoe leaves a print as you walk: a footstep is a footprint.

clue.text: Escape from work after striking

parts.note: workers on strike are out
to run a machine is to work or operate it

explanation.surface: Workers escape the office after walking out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only joins: the piece for work follows the piece for striking.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun pursuers is to get away from them by being faster.

clue.text: Out of tune, qualitatively different

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run tune, qualitatively

explanation.surface: Something out of tune is qualitatively different.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequal means not the same, so differing in size, amount or quality.

clue.text: Stays keen about county overlooked by daughter

indicators.note: the word for keen goes around the trimmed county

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is overlooked, so it is left out of the county

parts.note: Dorset is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone stays keen on a county, though their daughter overlooks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' is the noun: stiffened underwear, not 'remains'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are the boned bodice supports that make up corsets, collectively called corsetry.

clue.text: After treatment, lots going about in charge of a patient

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about the other pieces
after treatment the letters of lots are reshuffled

explanation.surface: After treatment, plenty of staff tend a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' is the adjective meaning uncomplaining, not a person in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoical means bearing hardship calmly, enduring without complaint.

clue.text: Expression when kissed reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard, not as written

parts.note: as means when, and pecked means kissed: together they sound like the entry

explanation.surface: Someone's look changes when kissed, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect can mean a facial expression or appearance.

clue.text: I enjoy discussing actions investor misconstrued

indicators.note: misconstrued suggests the letters of actions investor are read wrongly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys debating moves an investor has misread.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who loves talk could describe themselves this way: one who enjoys and excels at chat.

clue.text: In races need minute to send messages

indicators.note: the word for minute goes in between the races letters

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorbike race series
wee means tiny or minute

explanation.surface: In races you need a minute to send messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweet is to post short messages on the social site formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: One not heartless describing member with unpleasant rash

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
rude can mean unpleasant or offensive

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of not is removed

parts.note: taken as the word itself before trimming

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a member's nasty skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' at the end looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and imprudent are synonyms, both meaning acting without proper thought.

clue.text: Just defeat leaders of parties in poll

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters of parties, in and poll

explanation.surface: One party narrowly beats the others in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: To pip is to beat by a narrow margin, as in pipped at the post.

clue.text: Retired military commander caught shoplifting, say

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the commander's word is reversed

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler or commander

explanation.surface: A retired general is caught stealing from a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoplifting is one example of an offence against the law.

clue.text: Throw out old coat shortly

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: shortly means the word for coat is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur coat

explanation.surface: Someone discards a worn-out old coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to eject or force out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: First class work following conclusion of trial in tense case

indicators.note: the word for tense acts as a case, holding the other pieces

parts.note: tight means taut or tense
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: points to the last letter of trial

explanation.surface: First-rate work after a tense trial reaches its verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank or quality, the best category.
